1.explanation: The DataTable class is responsible for orchestrating both filtering and selection. Its getSelectionProps method wires up the header checkbox to the handleSelectAll (and the selectAll action) which naively toggles the selection state of every row in the full data set, ignoring the current filter state. To fix the bug, handleSelectAll (or the selectAll action it invokes) must be updated to only operate on the subset of rows that remain after filtering (i.e. the rows passed through defaultFilterRows/onInputChange), rather than the entire original list of rows.
1.bug_scenario: When the table is searched (filtered down to a subset of rows) and the header “Select All” checkbox is clicked, the component selects every row in the underlying data set (all 3 rows), rather than only the currently visible (filtered) row(s). The user expects “Select All” to only select the rows shown after filtering.

2.explanation: The DataTable component’s getSelectionProps method wires up both the row‐level and header ‘Select All’ checkboxes to internal actions. The selectAll action currently toggles the selection state for every row in the complete data set, regardless of filtering. To fix the bug, selectAll (and by extension getSelectionProps when used for the header) must be updated to only act on the subset of rows that remain after filterRows is applied (i.e., the visible rows passed into render()). This ensures that clicking Select All only selects the filtered rows, matching user expectations.
2.bug_scenario: After the user types a search term in the TableToolbarSearch, the table correctly filters down to only the matching rows. However, clicking the “Select All” checkbox in the table header still selects every row in the original data set (including those hidden by the filter). The expected behavior is that Select All only toggles the selection of the currently visible (filtered) rows.
